From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 May 2029 14:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal proposal + capacity upshift — legal input requested

All — quick take below. I kept language tight to avoid scope creep. Highlights:

1) EU data residency: Acceptable to represent that Customer data for EU-located end customers will be stored in EU regions, provided Customer selects "Dedicated" or "Private" deployment in the order form. Proposed clause: "For Customers with EU-resident end users, Redwood will provision and operate infrastructure within the EU region for the storage of Personal Data, subject to scheduled maintenance and emergency failover. Logs and aggregated telemetry may be processed outside the EU but will not contain Personal Data as defined in Section X."

2) SLA/credits: We can commit to 99.9% monthly availability for Dedicated clusters. Proposed addendum (to be appended to order form): a three-tier credit schedule (0.25% credit for each 0.1% below target, capped at 50% of monthly invoice).

3) Billing cadence: Finance will accept quarterly invoicing with net-30 but require a billing amendment executed alongside the order form to reflect invoicing frequency.

Next steps I recommend:
- Monica: send Anna a one-page summary with the three proposed legal bullets above and an updated OrderForm v1 -> v1.1 that shows Dedicated tick boxes and billing amendment line.
- I'll prepare a short MSA side-letter that captures the EU residency language and append the SLA schedule as an exhibit.

I'll keep the proposed language minimal so Clearwave counsel doesn't re-open unrelated indemnity or IP sections.

—Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference
